page: Amazon Web Services m8azn.12xlarge is a general-purpose, network- and EBS-optimized instance type built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor operating at up to 5.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning comprises 192.0 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no bundled local instance storage and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and standard compute engines. Network capabilities are provisioned with a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier execution across raw compute and memory throughput metrics. The instance records a single-core Geekbench score of 3127.0 and a multi-core score of 33041.0, paired with a multi-core stress-ng rating of 200882.59. Microarchitectural vector enhancements, including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, deliver high throughput in extended instruction tests, producing 149332.77 points in PassMark. Memory benchmarks register 529.59 GB/sec read bandwidth and 198.56 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks, driving strong caching and decompression performance such as 912.31 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The absence of local NVMe storage requires external EBS volumes for persistence, presenting an architectural tradeoff between local disk latency and managed storage flexibility. However, the high single-thread clock speed, 100 Gbps network pipe, and DDR5 throughput provide strong resource utilization and cost efficiency for large-scale enterprise services that avoid specialized GPU hardware. Benchmark validations indicate high efficiency for in-memory caching with 176.14 million Redis SET operations per second and 113.64 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The AWS m8azn.12xlarge is suited for network-heavy general-purpose workloads, distributed database clusters, memory-intensive caching tiers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks across small to medium language models.
description: Amazon Web Services m8azn.12xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance powered by a dedicated 48-core AMD EPYC 9R05 processor clocked up to 5.0 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System using the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 48 vCPUs with 1 thread per core and 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The system includes a 100 Gbps baseline network interface, has no local instance storage, and contains zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-core computing capability, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 33041.0 and Redis SET operation throughput reaching 176.14 million operations per second. Hardware vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX512_BF16 assist with high-throughput tasks. The m8azn.12xlarge is suited for network-intensive services, large in-memory key-value databases, distributed compilation, and CPU-based LLM inference.
